In Lisbon, Pablo had found the perfect flat: bright, near the metro, suspiciously cheap. The owner wrote beautifully. He was working abroad, he explained, and would post the keys once the deposit arrived. He even sent a photo of a passport.
"He sounds so genuine," said Pablo's flatmate Bilal. "Honestly, I trust him."
"I trust him too," Pablo said. "That's why I'm checking." He didn't judge the man's warmth; he checked what could be checked. The property register listed a different owner. The same kitchen photos appeared on a listing in another city. And the owner wouldn't agree to a video viewing.
Pablo reported the advert to the website and sent nothing. Bilal read the results over his shoulder. "He told it so smoothly," he said quietly.

qa.q: What did the property register show?
qa.a: The property register listed a different owner.

qa.q: What does Pablo mean by "I trust him too. That's why I'm checking"?
qa.a: Pablo feels warmly towards the owner but uneasy about how cheap the flat is, so he checks the facts rather than relying on that feeling.

qa.q: Which checks protected Pablo, and why were they better than a gut feeling?
qa.a: He checked the property register, the photos and whether a video viewing was possible; records and independent sources can't be charmed.

qa.q: How does Bilal's view of the owner change?
qa.a: Bilal moves from full trust to quiet surprise, realising a smooth, confident story was not a sign of truth.

grounding: An adult checks a flat owner's claims through records, photos and a viewing request instead of trusting how sincere the messages feel.

In the foundation's small office, Kunal and Vandana had two grant applications left. The first founder had pitched beautifully: tears at the right moment, a story about teaching three hundred girls. The second had stammered through her slides and apologised twice.
"The first one, surely," Vandana said. "She was so sincere."
"Maybe," Kunal said. "Let's check." He phoned the village school the first founder had named; the headmaster had never heard of her programme. The attendance sheets she sent had the same handwriting on every page. The second applicant's numbers matched the block office records, and a local teacher confirmed her classes by phone.
Vandana sat back. "I was ready to give it to the better storyteller."
"Practice makes a story smooth," Kunal said. "Only checking tells you it's true."

qa.q: What did the headmaster say about the first founder's programme?
qa.a: The headmaster had never heard of her programme.

qa.q: Why was Vandana ready to choose the first founder?
qa.a: Vandana was moved by the polished pitch and well-timed tears and took them as signs of sincerity.

qa.q: What did Kunal check, and why was it the right approach?
qa.a: He phoned the named school, looked closely at the attendance sheets, and matched the second applicant's numbers with block office records, relying on evidence rather than impressions.

qa.q: What would have happened to the second applicant if only the pitches had counted?
qa.a: She would likely have lost the grant despite real work, just for stammering and seeming less confident.

grounding: An adult verifies two grant claims through a phone call, documents and official records, finding that the most fluent story was the false one.

passage:
Subject: before you pay that agent

Dear Santosh,
I know you're excited about the job in Dubai, and I know the agent sounded wonderful on the phone. You said he knew everything, answered every question without a pause, and even cried a little talking about the workers he'd "helped." I believe he's good at talking. That's what worries me.
Last year, before I took my job, I stopped trusting how people sounded and started checking. Can you do the same?
Ask him for the company's full name and address in writing. Look it up yourself on the official government site for overseas jobs, not on a link he sends. Call the company's number from their own website and ask if the post exists. Ask two people who actually work there.
If everything matches, wonderful. If he gets angry at questions, that tells you something too.
Don't send anything until we've checked it together this weekend.
Trisha

qa.q: Where does Trisha tell Santosh to look up the company?
qa.a: On the official government site for overseas jobs, not on a link he sends.

qa.q: What is Trisha worried about in the agent's smooth phone manner?
qa.a: Trisha feels worried and uneasy that his fluent, emotional storytelling may come from practice rather than truth.

qa.q: What checks does Trisha advise before Santosh pays anything?
qa.a: Get the details in writing, check the official site, call the company's own number, ask real employees, and wait until they check together.

qa.q: How might Santosh feel reading the email?
qa.a: Santosh might feel a little deflated, but also cared for and safer, since Trisha is offering to check everything together first.

grounding: It shows an adult urging Santosh to verify an agent's claims through documents and independent sources instead of trusting his confident storytelling.

Bidisha, you'll laugh, but I'm quite proud of this. So on Saturday a man rings the bell. Very polite, ironed shirt, lanyard, a folder of photos of sick children. He talks beautifully. Not one pause. He knows my building's name, says my neighbour on the third floor already gave.
And I'm standing there, Lalit the softie, reaching for my wallet. He's so sincere.
Then I think: sincere is not a fact. Anyone can practise a speech.
So I ask to see his ID and the charity's registration number. He shows a card. I say, "Give me two minutes," and I look up the charity myself, find their number on their real website, and call. The lady there says they never collect door to door.
When I come back, he's gone. I told the society guard and posted a warning in our building group.
The kids need help. Just not through him.

qa.q: What did the lady at the charity say?
qa.a: The lady there says they never collect door to door.

qa.q: How did Lalit feel while the man was talking?
qa.a: Lalit felt moved and soft-hearted, even reaching for the wallet, because the man seemed so sincere.

qa.q: What steps helped Lalit check the claim?
qa.a: Lalit asked for ID and the registration number, looked up the charity himself and called the number on its real website, then warned the guard and neighbours.

qa.q: How might Bidisha react to Lalit's story?
qa.a: Bidisha would probably feel impressed and amused, and perhaps more careful about smooth talkers.

grounding: An adult describes checking a doorstep collector's claims through independent sources rather than trusting his fluent, sincere manner.

I work at the desk next to Minakshi in accounts, so I saw the whole thing on Monday.
A woman called Salma came in, confident and friendly, with a smart folder. She said she was from our biggest supplier and that their bank account had changed. She had a letter, a new account number and a very believable story about a bank merger. She even knew our purchase manager's name.
I was ready to update it. It all sounded so smooth.
Minakshi thanked her warmly, then said, "Let me just confirm with your office." She didn't call the number on Salma's letter. She took the supplier's number from our old contract file and dialled it.
The supplier's office had never heard of Salma. Their account hadn't changed.
When Minakshi put the phone down, Salma had already left. Minakshi reported it to our manager and the bank. I don't know what she felt, but her hands were very steady.

qa.q: Where did Minakshi get the supplier's number from?
qa.a: She took it from our old contract file.

qa.q: What might Minakshi have been thinking when she thanked Salma warmly?
qa.a: Minakshi was probably calm but cautious, polite on the surface while unwilling to trust a smooth story without checking.

qa.q: Which choice protected the company, and why?
qa.a: Calling the supplier on a number from the old contract instead of the one on Salma's letter, because an independent source cannot be faked by the visitor.

qa.q: How does the narrator see Salma's visit?
qa.a: The narrator found Salma's story so smooth that they were ready to update the account, which shows how convincing practised confidence can be.

grounding: A colleague observes an adult verifying a confident visitor's claim through an independent source rather than trusting her fluent story.

Monday: The visitor at the news desk told his story without a single pause: a relief drive after the floods, three hundred families fed, photos on his phone. Abhinav felt his chest warm; the man seemed so sincere. Afreen, the desk editor, only asked, "Registration papers? Names we can call?"
Wednesday: Abhinav laid his notes side by side. On Monday the drive had begun in August; in the man's follow-up email it began in July. The trust number he gave did not appear in the state register. Abhinav phoned the panchayat office of the village named, and the clerk said no such drive had come through.
The next Monday: Abhinav pinned a card above his desk: dates, documents, one independent voice. When a new intern gushed about a "really genuine" caller, Abhinav smiled. "The smoothest tellers are sometimes the most rehearsed. Let's check."

qa.q: Which month did the man's follow-up email give for the start of the drive?
qa.a: The man's follow-up email said the drive began in July, though on Monday it had begun in August.

qa.q: How did Abhinav feel while hearing the visitor's story on Monday?
qa.a: Abhinav felt warm and trusting; the story was fluent and moving, and the man seemed so sincere.

qa.q: Which checks worked, and why?
qa.a: Comparing dates across tellings, searching the state register and calling the panchayat office tested the claim against independent sources instead of the man's confident manner.

qa.q: How might a genuine relief volunteer see the desk's checks?
qa.a: A genuine volunteer would likely have papers and contacts ready and might welcome the checks, since verified coverage makes their work more believable.

grounding: Shows an adult learning to test claims through consistent dates, records and an independent call rather than a gut sense of the speaker's sincerity.
